Axiom:
Every finding carries a severity:
| Severity | Meaning | |---|---| | `BLOCKER` | task cannot be considered complete; merge forbidden | | `MAJOR` | behavior, required scope, remediation ownership, or verification is broken or cannot be proved; requires fix; allows merge only with explicit operator acceptance + Decision Log entry | | `MINOR` | mechanically fixable documentation, protocol, or style discrepancy that does not make behavior, scope, ownership, or verification ambiguous | | `INFO` | observation without mandatory action (often `INSIGHT_BACKFLOW`) |
Confidence constrains what severity may decide. `HIGH` and `MEDIUM` may participate in the verdict table. `LOW` is an unconfirmed observation: before summary, run one bounded independent check that can raise it to `MEDIUM`/`HIGH`; if it remains `LOW`, emit it only as `INFO`. A `LOW` finding never causes `FAIL`, opens an Execution Round, or authorizes an artifact change. It remains visible to the operator instead of becoming an interactive halt.
Severity does not depend on agent's mood or on whether the mismatch is in code or prose. Closed-world drift = `BLOCKER` by default; a coding-rules violation that can change behavior or verification = `MAJOR`; stylistic deviation = `MINOR`. A protocol or documentation mismatch is `MAJOR` only when it makes required behavior, scope, remediation ownership, or verification ambiguous or unprovable. Otherwise it is `MINOR` and cannot force another execution round. Distinguish that from new knowledge: a sound execution choice that preserves current requirements but suggests enriching canonical text is `INSIGHT_BACKFLOW` `INFO`, presented for optional operator review. A known canonical fact copied incorrectly into another artifact is documentation mismatch and remains `MINOR`. A claimed verification result with no executed evidence is not paper drift: it leaves required behavior unproved and is `MAJOR`.
**Overall status is computed from severities, never judged.** First matching row wins; print which row matched:
| Condition | Status | |---|---| | any open `BLOCKER` | `FAIL` | | any open `MAJOR` without operator acknowledgement | `FAIL` | | every open `MAJOR` acknowledged + Decision Log entry, and no `BLOCKER` | `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` | | only `MINOR` / `INFO`, or nothing | `PASS` |
`RULE_FILE_INCOMPLETE` and every other project-scope finding enters this table capped at `MINOR` (per `AX_FINDING_ROUTING`): shared infrastructure no task owns cannot decide that task's verdict. The `sev` field still reports the finding's own severity — the cap applies to the computation, not to the record.
This matters because the status is consumed mechanically: on PASS the audit records the round verdict; `[x] DONE` is already the phase's mechanical close. The audit remediates a progressing FAIL, and blocks only on evidenced no-progress or a real external decision. An unspecified verdict here makes those transitions arbitrary.
